stem: A university runs Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) in front of its on-premises Active Directory and has a single AWS account. IT staff must reach the AWS Management Console with their AD credentials, AD group membership must decide their permissions, and no IAM users may be created. What should the solutions architect configure?

choices.text: An Amazon Cognito identity pool that accepts AD FS assertions and exchanges them for IAM role credentials
An IAM SAML identity provider for AD FS, plus IAM roles that trust it and are mapped from AD groups
Create an Amazon Cognito user pool configured as a SAML service provider for AD FS, and use it for console sign-in
An AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory that replaces the on-premises forest and holds the staff accounts in AWS

rationale: SAML 2.0 federation lets users sign in through an IdP such as AD FS and reach the console without an IAM user for each person. You create a SAML identity provider in IAM, create roles whose trust policy names that provider, and configure AD FS assertions that map AD groups to the roles. A Cognito identity pool issues AWS credentials to users of your web or mobile app; it does not provide single sign-on to the AWS Management Console. A Cognito user pool authenticates users for your own applications and issues its own tokens; configuring it as a SAML service provider still only signs users into that application, not the AWS Management Console. AWS Managed Microsoft AD runs new domain controllers in your VPC; replacing the existing forest is a migration that the scenario does not call for and it still needs a federation or role mapping to reach the console.
